$comment: Independent scoring criteria for the Isolated Verifier step. The primary agent does NOT read this file during task execution — only the Verifier enforces these thresholds. This prevents the 'handoff tax' and 'collective delusion' failure modes identified in the MAST taxonomy (v2.0, 2026-05) and Anthropic's single-agent research (Oct 2026). Criteria are intentionally stricter than the CI merge-gate so the Verifier catches regressions the CI matrix misses.
name: Isolated Verifier Criteria

mechanical.description: Level 1 — deterministic, low-level correctness gates. These are the 'did it compile and run' checks.

openWeightsModels.description: Steal from AA Personality Bench rubric (FSX5FJS9PQ): test open-weights models off the shelf using trait indices as routing rubric, not leaderboard.

semantic.description: Level 2 — high-level objective alignment. These check 'does the output actually achieve the stated goal?' rather than just 'did the tests run'. This is the anti-MAST category-3 guard: independent verification against the original objective.

reviewTiers.description: Steal from GitHub Copilot code review tiers (Universe 2026): Lite, Balanced, Max. Each tier is a superset of the previous — Lite for fast everyday diffs, Balanced for normal development, Max for high-stakes changes requiring deep review. Mirrors GitHub's 'Lite and Balanced keep everyday reviews fast; Max provides a deeper look when a change needs it.'

lite.description: Fast everyday review — mechanical correctness gates only. Skip semantic checks to keep reviews fast.
lite.useIf: changes are small (< 100 LOC), low-risk, or the agent is in fast/single-file mode.

balanced.description: Everyday development balance — mechanical + semantic checks with standard thresholds.
balanced.useIf: default for PRs with medium risk or multi-file changes.

max.description: Deep review for high-stakes changes — mechanical + semantic + security + regression sweep at strictest thresholds.
max.useIf: changes touch security-sensitive paths, release-sensitive files, or have high regression risk.

gradingRubric.description: Canonical 100-point rubric for multi-agent swarm grading. Single source of truth — no dual rubrics. Deleted herdr-swarm variant (40/25/20/15) permanently on 2026-10-29.
gradingRubric.syncReason: Grading does not mint a passing candidate — --sync permanently refused.

goal_alignment.1.0: Changed files directly implement the stated goal; no unrelated changes.
goal_alignment.0.8: Changed files implement the core goal; minor tangential additions that don't distract.
goal_alignment.0.6: Changed files partially address the goal; significant portions missing.
goal_alignment.0.4: Changed files weakly relate to the goal; major gaps in implementation.
goal_alignment.0.0: Changed files do not address the stated goal at all.

edge_case_coverage.1.0: Tests cover normal, boundary, and error-path cases for the new logic.
edge_case_coverage.0.8: Tests cover normal and boundary cases; error paths partially covered.
edge_case_coverage.0.6: Tests cover normal cases only; boundary and error paths missing.
edge_case_coverage.0.4: Tests cover some normal cases but miss critical paths.
edge_case_coverage.0.0: No tests exist for the new logic.

regression_check.1.0: No existing tests regressed; all related test suites pass cleanly.
regression_check.0.8: No test failures but coverage dips slightly in touched areas.
regression_check.0.6: 1-2 minor test failures in unrelated areas (pre-existing).
regression_check.0.0: New test failures or regressions in related areas.

design_compliance.1.0: Implementation matches existing codebase patterns, conventions, and documented architecture.
design_compliance.0.8: Implementation mostly matches patterns; one minor convention deviation.
design_compliance.0.6: Implementation has notable pattern deviations but is internally consistent.
design_compliance.0.4: Implementation diverges significantly from documented patterns.
design_compliance.0.0: Implementation violates core architectural constraints or introduces anti-patterns.

isolation.description: The Verifier runs in a separate process with its own temp directory for proof artifacts — never sharing memory or context with the primary agent that wrote the code. This enforces the 'separate verifier that only runs tests and reports results' pattern from Anthropic's single-agent research.

budget.description: mabl-style Test Impact Analysis budget: cap total commands and wall-clock time across all mechanical checks. Skips remaining checks if exceeded (change-aware degradation).

qualityScore.description: Composite gate health score — mabl-style 'quality score' that surfaces verifier reliability before failures compound. Each must-pass check contributes equally; skips (via conditions or budget caps) reduce the score.

modelRouting.description: Ramp Laminar steal: harness-level model routing trims costs by assigning checks to local/fast models vs. cloud/capable models. modelHint on each check indicates the optimal tier. local = run on-device (no cloud cost), cloud = optional cloud offload for heavy semantic checks.

hints.local: Run on device using local resources (Laguna XS 2.1 / llama.cpp). No cloud cost.
hints.cloud: Route to hosted tier (Claude Opus / GPT-6) for heavy reasoning. Higher cost, higher accuracy.

personalityBench.description: AA Personality Bench (8 indices): Expressiveness, Organization, Informativeness, Transparency, Warmth, Conviction, Imagination, Slop. Route semantic checks to models matched by personality trait, not just raw intelligence. Analytical pushback checks need high Conviction + low Warmth; creative brainstorming needs high Imagination.

asyncExecution.description: Ramp Laminar + DeepInfer steal: 'Laminar lets agents keep working without waiting for every step to finish.' Independent mechanical checks with no inter-dependencies run in parallel when --parallel flag is set, reducing wall-clock latency. Budget caps (maxCommands, maxWallTimeMs) still apply globally. DeepInfer confidence-scheduled verification: when mechanical quality >= confidenceThreshold, skip non-critical semantic checks.
